tools.name: calendars_list
tools.title: List calendars
tools.description: List every calendar of every connected Outlook.com, Microsoft 365, Google, iCloud and calendar server account, each naming its account and provider, its calendarId, whether it is that account's default, whether the account owns it - one merely shared with it is not owned - and its owner's address, its access - edit, read, or freeBusy where Google lets only busy time be read - hidden where the person hid it from their Google list, its own time zone where Google keeps one - Outlook keeps none per calendar - and, under busyShownIn, each other account its busy time shows in. An account that could not be read, or whose events the person does not let you see, is named under unread with why, and one holding more calendars than one answer carries under cutShort. An account named under unread as needs_reconnection carries its own row under reconnectAt, where the person, signed in as the same account, presses "Reconnect"; calls to it answer again only once they have.

tools.name: events_list
tools.title: Read events
tools.description: Read what is on - the meetings, appointments and other events of a period, an agenda or schedule - across every connected calendar, earliest first, or latest first with newestFirst. query finds the events whose title, description, place, organizer or guests hold every word it names - a person by name or address included - on every account: Google searches its own, while Outlook, which searches titles alone, is read across the period and matched here. account, with provider where two share an address, reads that account alone, and calendarId, as calendars_list names it, that one of its calendars alone. Each event answers once, naming under copies every account and calendar holding it, with that copy's id, how it shows there and that account's own answer. An occurrence of a recurring series names under originalStart the start its series gave it, which a moved one keeps, and under each copy that account's seriesId. A calendar shared into one account from another connected account is read through its owner alone. Lumman's own busy copies - private blocks titled "Busy · <the address of the account it copies> (Multi Calendar connector)", on iCloud, which keeps no private events, or a calendar server, which may keep none, blocks titled "Busy (Multi Calendar connector)" - are never among the events: busyCopies answers them apart, one entry per copied busy time with its start and end, the account it copies under copyOf - unknown where no record of it stands - and each account it stands in under standsIn. None counts as the person's time or can be moved or cancelled; each is a busy copy of the account under copyOf, switched off by taking that pair away with busy_everywhere_set. Every time is given with its offset in the zone the answer names under timeZone: the one passed, else the person's stored zone, which now names with their time now; an all-day event's start and end are dates, its end the day after its last. An answer, a guest's or an account's own, is accepted, tentative, declined, unanswered or organizer, and one a copy cannot know is left out. An event names its kind where it is no ordinary event - a Google outOfOffice, focusTime, workingLocation, birthday or fromGmail entry - its privacy where it is not normal: public, private, confidential or personal - and its Teams, Zoom or Meet join link, and each copy its webLink; an out-of-office event shows as away. A description is its first 255 characters, marked descriptionCut where it goes on: events_get reads it. Where more events are read than one answer carries, the last in its order are left out and counted under leftOut with the period holding them all, which a narrower period or one calendar at a time reads further. A meeting whose guests alone one answer cannot carry names the first that fit, omittedAttendees counting the rest. Each calendar answers at most 50 events, read in time order; one with more is named under cutShort with its calendarId, readTo - the start of the last event read - and continueAt: passed with its account and calendarId, the same period and query, it reads on from exactly where it stopped; latest first, such a calendar's latest events are the ones past readTo, reached only by reading it on. A calendar or an account that could not be read, or that the person does not let you see, is named under unread with why: needs_reconnection, not_allowed, refused, gone, rate_limited or unavailable; where nothing could be read the answer is an error. An account named under unread as needs_reconnection carries its own row under reconnectAt, where the person, signed in as the same account, presses "Reconnect"; calls to it answer again only once they have. malformed counts events a provider sent in a form that could not be read, each left out. An event whose words screen as a prompt attack is left out and named under withheld by its start, its end and each copy's account, calendarId and id - by account alone where an id screened so - and a calendar whose name screened so is named by its account alone.

to.description: End of the period, excluded, in the same forms.

timeZone.description: An IANA zone such as Europe/London to answer in; the person's stored one where omitted.

query.description: Words, or a person by name or address, every one of which an event must hold.

newestFirst.description: true answers the latest events first.

tools.name: events_get
tools.title: Read an event
tools.description: Read one event whole, by the account, calendarId and id events_list names: its description as text - cut where one answer cannot carry it all, omittedCharacters counting what was left out, which reads at its web link - every Teams, Zoom or Meet join link found in the event, its place or its words, the organizer and each guest with their role - required, optional or resource - and answer, the first that fit where one answer cannot carry them all, omittedAttendees counting the rest; its kind and privacy as events_list names them, how it shows, the account's own answer, its reminders - the minutes before its start each sounds, or none, which events_edit writes as an empty list, and unsaid where a Google event keeps its calendar's own - and its web link. Times are given as events_list gives them, in the zone named under timeZone, and an occurrence of a recurring series its seriesId and originalStart as events_list names them. An event whose words screen as a prompt attack is withheld. One of Lumman's own busy copies is answered under busyCopy as events_list answers one, saying under about what it is and how it is switched off.

tools.name: free_times_find
tools.title: Find a time
tools.description: Find when the person is free or available - an open slot for a meeting, a call or an appointment - in every connected calendar: each stretch of a window that no busy time touches and that is at least as long as the meeting. An event holds its time as its provider's own free/busy shows it: on Google unless shown as available or declined - an invitation not yet answered or answered maybe included - on iCloud or a calendar server unless shown free or declined, and on Outlook only when shown busy or away, so an Outlook tentative answer leaves its time free; a cancelled event holds none. An all-day event holding time holds its whole day in the person's own time zone. The search never starts before now, keeps to every preference preferences_get names and to the window's first 365 days and, where the call names them, to hours on each day and to weekdays on top of those preferences; limit keeps the earliest stretches. Once any day has working hours, a day without them is off. The buffers pad the meeting being booked: a stretch starts buffer_before_minutes after busy time ends and ends buffer_after_minutes before the next begins. Each stretch answers once, in time order, with its parts inside the preferred times under preferred. Times, hours and weekdays are in the zone the call names, else the person's own; the stored working hours and preferred times are in the person's own. searched names the window searched and narrowedBy what narrowed it: notice, the least notice from now, rounded up to the quarter hour; horizon, to the end of its last day; yearCap, the 365 days; readLimit, a calendar holding more events than a search reads, read as far as it could be and searched to two days before the last it read; daysOff, days without working hours; fullDays, days already holding the most meetings in a day, a meeting being an event of some length that holds time inside that day's working hours. A calendar or account named under unread was not counted, nor were the calendars past the first 100 of an account under cutShort, so their busy time may fall inside a stretch. An account named under unread as needs_reconnection carries its own row under reconnectAt, where the person, signed in as the same account, presses "Reconnect"; calls to it answer again only once they have.

from.description: Start of the window, included, with its offset, e.g. 2026-10-12T09:00:00+01:00.

to.description: End of the window, excluded, with its offset.

minutes.description: Meeting length in minutes; the stored one where omitted.

timeZone.description: An IANA zone such as Europe/London the answer is given in; the stored one where omitted.

hours.description: Only these hours of each day, e.g. 10:00-16:00 or 09:00-12:00, 14:00-17:00.

weekdays.description: Only these days of the week.

limit.description: At most this many stretches, the earliest.

tools.name: events_create
tools.title: Create an event
tools.description: Create an event - schedule a meeting, book an appointment, block out time - in one of a connected account's own calendars: the one named by the calendarId calendars_list gives, else the account's default; a calendar only shared with the account is refused. Guests are invited by that account's provider: Microsoft or Google from the account's own address, Apple from its own address under the person's name, and a calendar server from the account's own address where it says it sends invitations, a meeting with guests refused elsewhere. A timed event's start and end are instants with their offset, the end no earlier than the start, so an entry of no length is taken; an all-day event's are dates, its end the day after its last. It is written in the person's own time zone, so an invitation shows that zone's time, and the answer gives its times in the zone it names under timeZone. A meeting with guests, no location and no video gets the person's default meeting link as its place. How it shows, its privacy, reminders, kind and video link are each refused with the reason where the account's provider lacks them. An Outlook subject takes at most 255 characters. repeat makes it a recurring series, each occurrence keeping the start's own hour in the person's time zone across clock changes. Who hears of it is notify's choice. Repeating a create whose answer was lost, with the same arguments, finds the event the first made rather than making a second - for the rest of that day (UTC), on Outlook only while Microsoft also recognises the repeat - so two events meant as two differ in some argument. Each guest's own times are answered under guestTimes in their time zone where it is known - the one guestZones names for them, else the one a member of the person's circles stored - and any other guest's zone as unknown, their time counted as the person's. A meeting any part of which falls, for a guest of known zone, outside 09:00-18:00 or on a Saturday or Sunday in that zone - an all-day one only on a Saturday or Sunday - is not sent: the refusal names each such guest and their time, and it goes out only once the call passes unusualHoursAgreed true on the person's word. A series is checked by its first occurrence; the person's own hours are never held.

repeat.description: Makes it a recurring series, from its start, without end unless until or count is named.

every.description: A month repeats on the start's day of the month, a year on its date.

until.description: The last date an occurrence may fall on.

tools.name: events_edit
tools.title: Change an event
tools.description: Change, move or reschedule an event the account organises, in place and in one call: its subject, body, location, start and end, how it shows, its privacy, reminders and video link, and its guests - addGuests invited, removeGuests taken off. Only what is named changes: the event keeps its id, every other guest's answer and its join link, a start named alone keeps its length and an end named alone keeps its start. Start and end are named as events_create names them, so naming both in the other form turns a timed event all-day or back, and are written in the person's own time zone as events_create writes them. What the account's provider lacks is refused with the reason, as on events_create, and so is a new body for an Outlook online meeting, whose join details it holds. Changing guests takes inviting allowed on the account. A whole series' start and end are its first occurrence's, and a change to a whole series holding occurrences changed apart from it is refused, naming each by when its series set it, so none of theirs is undone. Its provider sends a meeting's guests the change from the account's own address - Apple from its own address under the person's name, and a calendar server from the account's own address, to every guest, where it says it sends updates itself, a meeting with guests refused elsewhere - as notify chooses. Like every write, the answer names the event's provider, its calendarId where its provider addresses it by one, and its webLink. Guests' own hours hold a change as they hold events_create: every guest's where its times change, an added guest's at its time otherwise.

tools.name: events_cancel
tools.title: Cancel an event
tools.description: Cancel or call off an event the account organises; its provider sends a meeting's attendees the cancellation from that account's own address - Apple from its own address under the person's name, and a calendar server from the account's own address, to every guest, where it says it sends cancellations itself, a meeting with guests refused elsewhere - as notify chooses, and Outlook sends message with it. Someone else's event is not cancelled here: declining it with events_respond takes it off an Outlook calendar and leaves it on a Google one, shown declined. copyOnly true takes only the account's own copy of someone else's event off its calendar - an Outlook copy its organiser has cancelled included - sending nothing, though Google then shows the account as declined and so needs inviting and replying allowed.

tools.name: events_respond
tools.title: Answer an invitation
tools.description: Accept, tentatively accept or decline an invitation - an RSVP of yes, maybe or no; the account's provider sends the answer, with message where given, to its organiser from the account's own address unless notify is none. Answering a whole series answers each occurrence answered apart from it too, and says under replaced how many of their answers it replaced. In a calendar connected by its server's password, the server sends it where it says it sends answers itself - every time and with no message, so a call there naming a message or notify other than all is refused - and the answer is refused where it says no such thing. An invitation in an iCloud calendar is answered from its invitation letter or in Apple's own Calendar app, never here.

tools.name: busy_everywhere_set
tools.title: Show busy time everywhere
tools.description: Show one of an account's own calendars as busy in another connected account the person names, or stop: within seconds each busy event of the coming 60 days appears as a private block titled "Busy · <the calendar's account address> (Multi Calendar connector)" - on iCloud, which keeps no private events, or a calendar server, which may keep none, a block titled "Busy (Multi Calendar connector)" - in the main calendar of the account named, while it allows changing events - never in another calendar, and never in an account nobody named, one connected later included - one block per busy time however many calendars named into it hold it. A block moves with its event, goes when the event ends or goes or the pair is taken away, and is placed again if removed by hand; events_list answers blocks apart from events under busyCopies, and no tool counts, moves or cancels one. Naming a pair answers under shows the sentence to give the person word for word. calendars_list names each calendarId and the accounts each calendar already shows busy in.

tools.name: booking_links_create
tools.title: Make a booking link
tools.description: Make a booking link - a scheduling link offering times free_times_find found for a named meeting - for the person to send to one guest. The guest, with no account, picks one of these times in their own time zone and gives a name and address; the time is checked again against every calendar and the person's working hours, buffers, notice and daily maximum, and booked once, in the calendar the person named to receive bookings; a time no longer free is replaced by others up to the link's last, within those hours - Monday to Friday 09:00-17:00 where they stored none. The answer names the link's id and when it closes, 14 days after it is made, and a time after then is refused. The page a guest opens names nobody but the meeting, so subject is all a guest reads of whose meeting it is, e.g. Intro call with Sam Lee. An event holds its time as its provider's own free/busy shows it: on Google unless shown as available or declined - an invitation not yet answered or answered maybe included - on iCloud or a calendar server unless shown free or declined, and on Outlook only when shown busy or away, so an Outlook tentative answer leaves its time free; a cancelled event holds none.

subject.description: The meeting's name, as whoever opens the link reads it.

times.description: Each time offered, its start with its offset.

minutes.description: Meeting length in minutes; the stored one where omitted.

guestZone.description: The time zone of the guest the link is for, only as the person names it; the answer gives each time in it under guest too.

tools.name: booking_page_set
tools.title: Set up a booking page
tools.description: Set one of the person's permanent booking pages - a scheduling page anyone can book a time from - named by the name it answers at on this site: the one they hold by that name changes in the fields given alone, newName moving it to a new address while its old one answers nothing; a name they hold no page by adds a page, which needs subject and stays until the account goes. Anyone opening a page, with no account, sees up to 20 times free in every calendar within the person's working hours - Monday to Friday 09:00-17:00 where they stored none - and every other preference, spread across the coming 14 days, each day's preferred times first, in their own time zone, and books one by giving a name and address, in the calendar the person named to receive bookings; a time is booked once across all their pages. The page a guest opens names nobody but the meeting, so subject is all a guest reads of whose meeting it is, e.g. Intro call with Sam Lee. An event holds its time as its provider's own free/busy shows it: on Google unless shown as available or declined - an invitation not yet answered or answered maybe included - on iCloud or a calendar server unless shown free or declined, and on Outlook only when shown busy or away, so an Outlook tentative answer leaves its time free; a cancelled event holds none.

name.description: The page's name in its address: 3 to 40 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.

newName.description: A new name for the page named, which its address then carries.

subject.description: The meeting's name, as the guest reads it; a new page needs it.

minutes.description: Meeting length in minutes; for a new page the stored one where omitted.

tools.name: polls_create
tools.title: Make a group poll
tools.description: Make a group poll of times free_times_find found for a named meeting, for the people it is for to vote on the times they can make. Each address gets its own link, an address named twice one, handed back in this answer alone - a lost link needs a new poll. Lumman sends them nothing: the person shares the links, or each goes from the person's own mailbox. Whoever opens a link, with no account, ticks the times that address can make, answering again replaces its answer, and sees no one else's. polls_results ranks the times and polls_book books one, in the calendar the person named to receive bookings, which making a poll does not need; a poll closes once booked, or 14 days after it is made, and then holds no address or answer. Naming a circle makes a poll for members of it or, on the person's own circle, for addresses invited that have not joined, meant for those circles_free_times_find names under noCalendar or notJoined: once they answer, the person's own searches for that circle count each by the times they can make, and their page offers to connect a calendar - an address that has not joined joins first, through the letter circles_invite sent it. A member with a calendar is read through it, never from a poll. The page a guest opens names nobody but the meeting, so subject is all a guest reads of whose meeting it is, e.g. Intro call with Sam Lee. An invitee whose time zone is known, as events_create knows a guest's, is answered with that zone and each time in it.

subject.description: The meeting's name, as whoever opens the link reads it.

times.description: Each time offered, its start with its offset.

minutes.description: Meeting length in minutes; the stored one where omitted.

invitees.description: The address of each person the poll is for.

tools.name: polls_results
tools.title: Read a poll's answers
tools.description: Read a poll's answers: each of its times still to come with the addresses of those who can make it, most first, then each address it is for and whether it has answered. An answer is what that address's own link sent. A booked or closed poll holds none; booked names the time it was booked, or is being booked, at. Its times are in the zone stored when it was made.

poll.description: The poll's id, as polls_create names it.

tools.name: polls_book
tools.title: Book a poll's time
tools.description: Book one of a poll's times in the calendar the person named to receive bookings: the time is checked again against every calendar, exactly the people the poll is for are invited by Microsoft or Google from that account's own address, by Apple from its own address under the person's name, or by its calendar server from the account's own address, the meeting written in the person's own time zone, and the poll closes. Its invitees' own hours hold it as they hold events_create, save for one who ticked that time, chosen on their own clock. An event holds its time as its provider's own free/busy shows it: on Google unless shown as available or declined - an invitation not yet answered or answered maybe included - on iCloud or a calendar server unless shown free or declined, and on Outlook only when shown busy or away, so an Outlook tentative answer leaves its time free; a cancelled event holds none.

poll.description: The poll's id, as polls_create names it.

start.description: The time to book, as polls_results names it.

guestZones.description: A guest's own time zone, only as the person names it - never inferred from an address, a language or a provider.

unusualHoursAgreed.description: True only once the person has agreed to send at the hours an answer named as unusual for a guest.

tools.name: links_polls_list
tools.title: List open links and polls
tools.description: List the person's booking links and group polls still open or being booked, oldest first - each link with its id, meeting, state, when it closes and the times it still offers, each poll with its id, meeting, state, who it is for, how many have answered and the times someone can make, most first - every booking page with its address, and every booking a link, poll or page took for a time 30 days ago or later, never who booked it. One being booked for longer than a booking takes is stuck, and links_polls_close closes it. polls_results reads a poll's answers. A link's or a poll's times are in the zone stored when it was made.

tools.name: links_polls_close
tools.title: Close a link or poll
tools.description: Close one of the person's booking links or group polls still open or being booked: its page answers closed from then on, and a poll's addresses and answers are deleted. A meeting the provider made for one being booked stays: events_list shows whether it was. links_polls_list names each.

id.description: The link's or poll's id, as links_polls_list names it.

tools.name: circles_invite
tools.title: Invite people into a circle
tools.description: Invite people by address - family, friends or a team, who share when they are busy once they join - into one of the person's own circles: an existing one by its id, as circles_list names it, or one by its name, matched whatever its case and made where the person has none by it - two of the person's circles whose names differ only in case are refused, naming both ids. Lumman emails each address newly invited a letter under the person's address, replies going to them, naming the circle and saying how to join; only an account signed in at that address can join. A circle's name that screens as a prompt attack sends nothing. The answer names the circle's id, whether it was made, each address sent a letter under invited, each already invited there - sent nothing new - under kept, and under unsent each whose letter could not go, which was not invited. An account sends at most 20 such letters in any 24 hours, those sent from its page included; a call asking for more than remain invites nobody and says how many can go and when more free.

circle.description: An existing circle's id, as circles_list names it.

name.description: The circle's name, where no id is passed.

tools.name: circles_list
tools.title: List circles
tools.description: List every circle the person owns or has joined: its id, its name, whether it is the person's own, the address of each member who has joined and, on the person's own, of each address invited that has not joined under invited. circles_free_times_find finds a time for one.

tools.name: circles_free_times_find
tools.title: Find a time for a circle
tools.description: Find when everyone in one of the person's circles - family, friends or a team - is free or available: each stretch of a window that no member's busy time touches and that is at least as long as the meeting, in the zone the call names, else the person's own - the same whichever member asks, save for a member with no calendar connected, counted by the asker's own polls. The calendars each member owns and counts as busy - never one someone else shared with them - are read through that member's own connection as the call is made, and come back under busy only as when that member is busy - the circle's owner named owner, every other member by the address invited - never what an event says. An event holds its time as its provider's own free/busy shows it: on Google unless shown as available or declined - an invitation not yet answered or answered maybe included - on iCloud or a calendar server unless shown free or declined, and on Outlook only when shown busy or away, so an Outlook tentative answer leaves its time free; a cancelled event holds none. An all-day event holding time holds its whole day in its member's time zone; no one's stored working hours or other preferences apply, only the hours and weekdays the call names, in the answer's zone; limit keeps the earliest stretches, and the search keeps to the window's first 365 days. A member none of whose calendars could be read is named under unknown, and one only some of whose could under readInPart, their busy time read counted; either's busy time may fall inside a stretch. A member with no calendar connected counts as free only at the times they ticked in the person's own polls for this circle, and until they answer one is named under noCalendar - polls_create naming the circle asks them. On the person's own circle each address invited that has not joined is named under notJoined and counts the same way once it answers such a poll. Anyone counted by polls whose answers tick no time in the window is named under tickedNothing. Each stretch names under members every other member's own time for it in the zone they stored, marked unusual where any of it falls outside 09:00-18:00 or on a Saturday or Sunday there. circles_list names each circle's id. Any of the person's own accounts needing reconnection is named under unread, another member's never. An account named under unread as needs_reconnection carries its own row under reconnectAt, where the person, signed in as the same account, presses "Reconnect"; calls to it answer again only once they have.

circle.description: The circle's id, as circles_list names it.

from.description: Start of the window, included, with its offset, e.g. 2026-10-12T09:00:00+01:00.

to.description: End of the window, excluded, with its offset.

minutes.description: Meeting length in minutes; the stored one where omitted.

timeZone.description: An IANA zone such as Europe/London the answer is given in; the stored one where omitted.

hours.description: Only these hours of each day, e.g. 10:00-16:00 or 09:00-12:00, 14:00-17:00.

weekdays.description: Only these days of the week.

limit.description: At most this many stretches, the earliest.
